2027-01-28.title: Fourth Thursday of Denha · St Thomas Aquinas
2027-01-28.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: The love of Christ urges us on
The call of the first disciples
2027-01-28.alt: Season of Denha. St Thomas Aquinas: 1 Kings 3:5–12; Wisdom 7:7–14; 1 Corinthians 1:18–25; Matthew 5:13–16.
2027-01-28.verse: For the love of Christ urges us on, because we are convinced that one has died for all; therefore all have died.
theo: Paul explains to the Corinthians what drives him. Some boast “in outward appearance and not in the heart”; he has a different motive: “For the love of Christ urges us on, because we are convinced that one has died for all; therefore all have died.” Christ's love is not only something Paul feels for Christ; it is Christ's own love for him, pressing on him like a current, carrying him toward others. In the Gospel that love begins with a glance and a question. John the Baptist sees Jesus walking by and exclaims, “Look, here is the Lamb of God!” Two disciples follow. Jesus turns and asks them, “What are you looking for?” They answer with another question, calling him Rabbi, Teacher: “where are you staying?” He says, “Come and see.” They stay with him that day; John even remembers the hour, about four o'clock in the afternoon. Andrew then finds his brother: “We have found the Messiah”, and Jesus looks at Simon and gives him a new name, Cephas. Denha shows us how Christ is made known: one person tells another, and Christ himself does the rest.

Today the Church honours St Thomas Aquinas, the Dominican friar whose great mind served the faith. He taught that reason can prepare the way, but only faith receives the truth that Christ is the Son of God, and he wrote that grace does not destroy nature but perfects it. His whole work answered Jesus' first question, “What are you looking for?” According to the early accounts of his life, he heard the Lord ask him in prayer what reward he wanted for all he had written, and he answered: nothing but you, Lord. Near the end of his life, after an experience at the Holy Qurbana, he stopped writing and said that all he had written seemed like straw beside what he had seen. Like the first disciples, he came, saw, and remained. The love of Christ urged him on.

2027-01-28.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, Lamb of God, you asked your first disciples what they were looking for and invited them to come and see. Let your love urge us on, make us bring others to you as Andrew brought Simon, and through the prayers of St Thomas Aquinas give us minds that seek you and hearts that want nothing but you. Amen.

illus: A college student in Thrissur, preparing for exams, pasted a small card above her desk with a prayer of St Thomas Aquinas for study. Her room-mate, who never went to church, asked what it meant. The answer led to a long conversation, and a few months later the room-mate came with her to the Sunday Qurbana. Come and see, the student said later, is still the best invitation.

homily: Dear friends, Paul says: the love of Christ urges us on, because we are convinced that one has died for all (2 Corinthians 5:14). Christ's love is like a current that carries us toward others.

In the Gospel John points to Jesus: look, here is the Lamb of God! Two disciples follow. Jesus turns and asks: what are you looking for? (John 1:38). They ask where he is staying, and he says: come and see. They remain with him that day.
Then Andrew finds his brother Simon and says: we have found the Messiah (John 1:41). He brings him to Jesus, who gives him a new name. This is how Christ is made known: one person tells another.

St Thomas Aquinas, whom we honour today, gave his great mind to Christ. The early accounts tell that when the Lord asked him what reward he wanted, he answered: nothing but you, Lord. May we too seek nothing but Christ, and bring others to him. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus asked two friends: what are you looking for? Then he said: come and see! Who can you invite to come and see Jesus?

q: One thing I asked of the LORD, that will I seek after: to live in the house of the LORD all the days of my life, to behold the beauty of the LORD, and to inquire in his temple.
When Jesus turned and saw them following, he said to them, “What are you looking for?” They said to him, “Rabbi” (which translated means Teacher), “where are you staying?”

q: O taste and see that the LORD is good; happy are those who take refuge in him.
